<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="runtime-foundations"><a href="#runtime-foundations">Runtime foundations</a></h2>

The reviewed README describes ABI as a nightly Rust framework for local AI service orchestration, WDBX semantic storage, and runtime primitives. It explicitly says that the older Zig tree was removed.

CLI and MCP surfaces are documented alongside local inspection commands. Their presence does not independently establish successful live-provider dispatch, general model quality, or every transport integration. Use the relevant contract and current source when evaluating one of those behaviors.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="capability-is-not-execution"><a href="#capability-is-not-execution">Capability is not execution</a></h2>

A capability table can identify a preferred backend without proving that its native kernels are linked. ABI’s README requires honest accelerated=false reporting in that situation and describes deterministic CPU SIMD fallback.

Do not turn that fallback into a GPU speedup claim. CUDA, Vulkan, and ANE native-kernel claims require their own evidence. Hardware availability, linking, execution, correctness, and performance are separate questions.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="demos-have-boundaries"><a href="#demos-have-boundaries">Demos have boundaries</a></h2>

The project’s benchmark dashboard renders synthetic sample data. It can demonstrate a presentation format, but those charts are not measured throughput, latency, or accuracy. The small neural demonstration is not a production LLM.

The README also distinguishes local browser planning from actual autonomous browser execution. Treat plans and reference surfaces as what they are, and follow the documented external-integration boundary rather than claiming an embedded browser.

</section>
